passages.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian church.
Paul is an apostle.
Paul is free.
Paul has seen Jesus Christ, who is our Lord.
The Corinthian believers are the result of Paul's work in the Lord.
Paul calls the Corinthians his workmanship in Christ.
passages.original: Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐλεύθερος οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος οὐχὶ Ἰησοῦν τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν ἑόρακα οὐ τὸ ἔργον μου ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Some people do not accept Paul as an apostle.
You, the believers in Corinth, do accept Paul as an apostle.
You are proof that Paul is truly an apostle.
Your faith in the Lord shows that Paul’s work is genuine.
You are the seal of Paul’s apostleship in the Lord.
passages.original: εἰ ἄλλοις οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος ἀλλά γε ὑμῖν εἰμι ἡ γὰρ σφραγίς μου τῆς ἀποστολῆς ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: This is my defense to those who scrutinize me: Have we no right to food and to drink?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Some people question Paul’s authority.
Paul gives a defense to these people.
Paul asks a question.
Paul says, “Do we not have the right to eat?”
Paul says, “Do we not have the right to drink?”
passages.original: Ἡ ἐμὴ ἀπολογία τοῖς ἐμὲ ἀνακρίνουσίν ἐστιν αὕτη μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν

passages.text: Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the Corinthians.
Paul asks a question about his rights as an apostle.
Paul says, “Do we not have the right to take along a believing wife?”
Other apostles take along believing wives.
The Lord’s brothers take along believing wives.
Cephas, also called Peter, takes along a believing wife.
Paul asks if he and his companions have the same right as these others.
passages.original: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ἀδελφὴν γυναῖκα περιάγειν ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ Κηφᾶς

passages.text: Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?
passages.sermon:
Barnabas and I are apostles.
We serve Jesus Christ.
Do only Barnabas and I lack the right to refrain from working for a living?
Do other apostles have this right?
Are we the only ones who must support ourselves by working?
Other apostles do not have to work for their living.
Barnabas and I must work to support ourselves.
Is this fair?
Do we not have the same right as the other apostles?
passages.original: ἢ μόνος ἐγὼ καὶ Βαρνάβας οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν μὴ ἐργάζεσθαι

passages.text: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?
passages.sermon:
A soldier does not pay his own expenses.
A soldier receives support while he serves.
A person who plants a vineyard eats the fruit from it.
A person who tends a flock drinks the milk from the flock.
People who work in these ways share in the benefits of their work.
passages.original: Τίς στρατεύεται ἰδίοις ὀψωνίοις ποτέ τίς φυτεύει ἀμπελῶνα καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐσθίει ἢ τίς ποιμαίνει ποίμνην καὶ ἐκ τοῦ γάλακτος τῆς ποίμνης οὐκ ἐσθίει

passages.text: Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul asks a question.
He says, “Am I speaking only from a human point of view?”
He asks another question.
He says, “Doesn’t the Law also say the same thing?”
passages.original: Μὴ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ταῦτα λαλῶ ἢ καὶ ὁ νόμος ταῦτα οὐ λέγει

passages.text: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
passages.sermon:
The Law of Moses contains a command from God.
God says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.”
God gave this command in the Scriptures.
God is not only concerned about oxen.
God’s concern is not just for animals.
passages.original: ἐν γὰρ τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ γέγραπται Οὐ κημώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα μὴ τῶν βοῶν μέλει τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words for us.
God did not write them only for oxen.
God wrote them for our sake.
The plowman works the field.
He should expect to receive a share of the harvest.
The thresher works to separate the grain.
He should also expect to receive a share of the harvest.
passages.original: ἢ δι’ ἡμᾶς πάντως λέγει δι’ ἡμᾶς γὰρ ἐγράφη ὅτι ὀφείλει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ὁ ἀροτριῶν ἀροτριᾶν καὶ ὁ ἀλοῶν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν

passages.text: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and his companions taught you spiritual truths.
They gave you the message of God.
They shared the gospel with you.
They planted spiritual seed among you.
Is it too much if they receive material help from you?
Is it too much if they reap a material harvest from you?
They gave you spiritual blessings.
It is right for them to receive material support in return.
passages.original: Εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν τὰ πνευματικὰ ἐσπείραμεν μέγα εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῶν τὰ σαρκικὰ θερίσομεν

passages.text: If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and his companions preach the gospel to the Corinthians.
Some people have the right to receive support from the Corinthians.
Paul and his companions have this right even more.
Paul and his companions did not use this right.
They chose to endure everything.
They did this so that nothing would hinder the gospel of Christ.
passages.original: εἰ ἄλλοι τῆς ὑμῶν ἐξουσίας μετέχουσιν οὐ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐχρησάμεθα τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ταύτῃ ἀλλὰ πάντα στέγομεν ἵνα μή τινα ἐνκοπὴν δῶμεν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?
passages.sermon: Those who work in the temple eat food from the temple.\r\nThose who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar.
passages.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ τὰ ἱερὰ ἐργαζόμενοι τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐσθίουσιν οἱ τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ παρεδρεύοντες τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ συμμερίζονται

passages.text: In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.
passages.sermon:
The Lord gave a command.
He gave this command to people who preach the gospel.
The Lord said these preachers should get their living from the gospel.
Preachers of the gospel should receive support through their work of preaching.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ὁ Κύριος διέταξεν τοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον καταγγέλλουσιν ἐκ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ζῆν

passages.text: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul has certain rights as a preacher of the gospel.
\r\nI have not used any of these rights.
\r\nI am not writing this to ask for anything to be done for me.
\r\nI would rather die than lose my reason to boast.
\r\nNo one will take away my boast.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ κέχρημαι οὐδενὶ τούτων οὐκ ἔγραψα δὲ ταῦτα ἵνα οὕτως γένηται ἐν ἐμοί καλὸν γάρ μοι μᾶλλον ἀποθανεῖν ἢ τὸ καύχημά μου οὐδεὶς κενώσει

passages.text: Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul preaches the gospel.
Paul does not have a reason to boast when he preaches the gospel.
Paul must preach the gospel.
God has given Paul this duty.
If Paul does not preach the gospel, he faces great trouble.
Paul says, "Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel."
passages.original: Ἐὰν γὰρ εὐαγγελίζωμαι οὐκ ἔστιν μοι καύχημα ἀνάγκη γάρ μοι ἐπίκειται οὐαὶ γάρ μοί ἐστιν ἐὰν μὴ εὐαγγελίσωμαι

passages.text: If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul preaches the gospel.
\r\nIf I preach the gospel willingly, I receive a reward.
\r\nIf I do not preach willingly, God still gives me a responsibility.
\r\nGod entrusts me with the task of preaching, even if I do not choose it.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἑκὼν τοῦτο πράσσω μισθὸν ἔχω εἰ δὲ ἄκων οἰκονομίαν πεπίστευμαι

passages.text: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul preaches the gospel.
Paul asks, "What is my reward?"
Paul answers his question.
Paul says, "My reward is this."
Paul offers the gospel free of charge.
Paul does not use his rights as a preacher of the gospel.
passages.original: τίς οὖν μού ἐστιν ὁ μισθός ἵνα εὐαγγελιζόμενος ἀδάπανον θήσω τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς τὸ μὴ καταχρήσασθαι τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ

passages.text: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul is free from obligation to all people.
Paul chooses to serve everyone as a slave.
Paul does this to win as many people as possible to Christ.
passages.original: Ἐλεύθερος γὰρ ὢν ἐκ πάντων πᾶσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα ἵνα τοὺς πλείονας κερδήσω

passages.text: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul wants to win people for Christ.
Paul speaks about his approach to different groups.
I became like a Jew to the Jews.
I did this to win the Jews.
I became like one under the law to those under the law.
I am not myself under the law.
I did this to win those under the law.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγενόμην τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὡς Ἰουδαῖος ἵνα Ἰουδαίους κερδήσω τοῖς ὑπὸ νόμον ὡς ὑπὸ νόμον μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ὑπὸ νόμον ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον κερδήσω

passages.text: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul serves Christ and preaches the gospel.
Paul meets many different people.
Some people do not have the law of Moses.
Paul acts like someone without the law of Moses when he is with them.
Paul does this to reach people who do not have the law of Moses.
Paul himself is not without the law of God.
Paul lives under the law of Christ.
Paul does this so he can win those who do not have the law of Moses.
passages.original: τοῖς ἀνόμοις ὡς ἄνομος μὴ ὢν ἄνομος Θεοῦ ἀλλ’ ἔννομος Χριστοῦ ἵνα κερδάνω τοὺς ἀνόμους

passages.text: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul wanted to share the gospel with everyone.
Paul saw some people who were weak.
Paul became like the weak.
Paul did this to win the weak.
Paul became all things to all people.
Paul did this so that he might save some people by any possible means.
passages.original: ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν ἀσθενής ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσω τοῖς πᾶσιν γέγονα πάντα ἵνα πάντως τινὰς σώσω

passages.text: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul acts for a clear purpose.
\r\nPaul does everything for the sake of the gospel.
\r\nPaul wants to share in the blessings of the gospel.
passages.original: Πάντα δὲ ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἵνα συνκοινωνὸς αὐτοῦ γένωμαι

passages.text: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Corinthians.
He uses the example of a race.
In a race, many runners compete.
All the runners run.
Only one runner receives the prize.
Paul tells the Corinthians to run like that one runner.
Run in such a way that you may win the prize.
passages.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἐν σταδίῳ τρέχοντες πάντες μὲν τρέχουσιν εἷς δὲ λαμβάνει τὸ βραβεῖον οὕτως τρέχετε ἵνα καταλάβητε

passages.text: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.
passages.sermon:
Everyone who competes in the games uses strict discipline.
They control themselves in all things.
They do this to win a crown that will not last.
We do this to win a crown that will last forever.
passages.original: πᾶς δὲ ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος πάντα ἐγκρατεύεται ἐκεῖνοι μὲν οὖν ἵνα φθαρτὸν στέφανον λάβωσιν ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄφθαρτον

passages.text: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking about his own actions and discipline.
I run with purpose.
I do not run without a clear goal.
I fight with intention.
I do not fight as if I am only striking the air.
passages.original: ἐγὼ τοίνυν οὕτως τρέχω ὡς οὐκ ἀδήλως οὕτως πυκτεύω ὡς οὐκ ἀέρα δέρων

passages.text: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul is a Christian apostle.
\r\nPaul disciplines his body.
\r\nPaul makes his body his slave.
\r\nPaul does this so he will not be disqualified.
\r\nPaul has preached to others.
\r\nPaul wants to avoid being disqualified after preaching to others.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπωπιάζω μου τὸ σῶμα καὶ δουλαγωγῶ μή πως ἄλλοις κηρύξας αὐτὸς ἀδόκιμος γένωμαι
